# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |
| github.com/BurntSushi/toml                | v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64   | v0.3.1                             | true   | true             |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory
        (Use -mod=mod or -mod=readonly to bypass.)
```

The following will work:

```
go list -u -m -mod=mod -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -mod=readonly -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

### Docker

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated
```

To use parameters just append:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated -update
```

### CI pipelines

Using the -ci flag will make the command exit with non-zero code, breaking your CI pipelines if outdated dependencies are found.

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail if **any direct or indirect** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -ci
```

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail **only if a direct** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -ci
```

### Command-line flags

Use the **-h** or **-help** flag to see all available options:

```
$ go-mod-outdated -help

Usage of go-mod-outdated:
  -direct
        List only direct modules
  -update
        List only modules with updates
  -ci
        Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found
  -style string
        Output style, pass 'markdown' for a Markdown table (default "default")
```

### Shortcut aliases

If **go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct** seems too difficult to remember, you can create shortcuts using aliases:

```
alias gmo="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated"

alias gmod="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct"

alias gmou="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update"

alias gmodu="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -update"
```  

## Understanding the output

### VALID TIMESTAMPS column

There are cases where the updated version reported by the go list command is actually older than the current one. go-mod-outdated includes a **VALID TIMESTAMPS** column which indicates when this happens, helping you avoid upgrading to a version that might break your application.

### Important note about upgrading

Upgrading an application is the responsibility of the application maintainer. Semantic versioning provides a way to indicate breaking changes, but everything relies on each module developer applying correct version tags. Unless there is a fully automated way to detect breaking changes in a codebase, a good practice to avoid surprises is to write tests and avoid dependencies on modules that are not well maintained and documented.

p=run("NOTJSON\n",["-ci"])
print("ci invalid",p.returncode, repr(p.stdout), repr(p.stderr))

inp2='{"Path":"a.com/x","Version":"v1","Time":"2020-01-01T00:00:00Z","Update":{"Path":"a.com/x","Version":"v2"}}\n'
p=run(inp2,["-ci"])
print("ci panic",p.returncode, repr(p.stdout.decode()), repr(p.stderr.decode()[:2000]))

# Mix direct/indirect with ci to determine filtered vs unfiltered
def mk(o): return json.dumps(o)
direct_noupd={"Path":"a.direct","Version":"v1"}
indirect_upd={"Path":"a.indirect","Version":"v1","Indirect":True,"Update":{"Version":"v2"}}
indirect_noupd={"Path":"a.indirect","Version":"v1","Indirect":True}
direct_upd={"Path":"a.direct","Version":"v1","Update":{"Version":"v2"}}
combos=[
 ([direct_noupd,indirect_upd],["-ci"]),
 ([direct_noupd,indirect_upd],["-ci","-direct"]),
 ([direct_noupd,indirect_upd],["-ci","-update"]),
 ([direct_noupd,indirect_upd],["-ci","-direct","-update"]),
 ([direct_upd,indirect_noupd],["-ci","-direct"]),
 ([direct_upd,indirect_noupd],["-ci","-update"]),
 ([direct_noupd,indirect_noupd],["-ci"]),
 # main upd + direct noupd
 ([{"Path":"main","Version":"v1","Main":True,"Update":{"Version":"v2"}}, direct_noupd],["-ci"]),
 ([{"Path":"main","Version":"v1","Main":True,"Update":{"Version":"v2"}}, direct_noupd],["-ci","-update"]),
]
for objs,args in combos:

import subprocess, json
def run(inp,args=[]):
    return subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args,input=inp.encode(),capture_output=True)
def show(desc,obj,args=[]):
    p=run(json.dumps(obj)+"\n",args)
    lines=p.stdout.decode().splitlines()
    row=lines[3] if len(lines)>3 else repr(p.stdout.decode())
    print(f"{desc} args={args} exit={p.returncode} row={row!r} err={p.stderr.decode()!r}")

show("Versions several", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Versions":["v1","v2","v3"]})
show("Versions several -update", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Versions":["v1","v2","v3"]},["-update"])
show("Versions several -ci", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Versions":["v1","v2","v3"]},["-ci"])
show("Replace Versions", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"Versions":["v9","v10"]}})
show("Replace Dir only", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"Dir":"/tmp/local","Path":"../local"}})
show("Replace Dir+Version empty", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"Dir":"/tmp/local","Version":""}})
show("Replace GoVersion", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"GoVersion":"1.21"}})
show("Replace Error", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"Error":{"Err":"boom"}}})
show("Error with Update", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Error":{"Err":"boom"},"Update":{"Version":"v2"}})
show("Error Err empty", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Error":{"Err":""}})
show("GoVersion/Dir/GoMod set", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","GoVersion":"1.21","Dir":"/tmp","GoMod":"/tmp/go.mod"})
# Nested versions in Update/Replace effect on New Version?
show("Update Versions", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Update":{"Versions":["v2","v3"]}})
show("Replace.Update Versions", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":{"Version":"v9","Update":{"Versions":["vR"]}}})

# Replace null vs present distinguishing based on pointer
show("Replace null", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Replace":None})
show("Update null Replace update", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Update":None,"Replace":{"Version":"v9","Update":{"Version":"vR"}}})
show("Update null Replace update -update", {"Path":"x","Version":"v1","Update":None,"Replace":{"Version":"v9","Update":{"Version":"vR"}}},["-update"])

# Does -update filter use original Update even if null explicitly? JSON null to pointer sets nil.

# Interaction: Main inside Replace/Update etc already

# Interaction: module with Main true but replace ?? already filtered based original.
# What about module where Path is main (?) name? no.

PY
"}

import subprocess, json
def run_str(s, col="Path"):
    obj={"Path":"x","Version":"v1"}
    obj[col]=s
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"],input=(json.dumps(obj)+"\n").encode(),capture_output=True)
    return p.stdout.decode()

def cells(s,col="Path"):
    out=run_str(s,col)
    lines=out.splitlines()
    if not lines: return []
    border=lines[0]
    # data lines between header separator (line 2 index) and final border
    data=lines[3:-1]
    # first column content between first and second |, strip one leading space and trailing pad?
    idx=1 if col=="Path" else 2
    result=[]
    for l in data:
        parts=l.split("|")
        if len(parts)>idx:
            result.append(parts[idx])
    return border.split("+")[idx], result

tests=[
 "a"*29, "a"*30, "a"*31, "a"*32, "a"*60,
 "a "*20,   # trailing space
 " ".join(["word"]*10),
 " ".join(["a"]*40),
 " ".join(["abcdefghij"]*5),
 " ".join(["abcdefghij"]*3),
 " ".join(["abcdefghijklmno"]*3),
 "hello world "*5,
 "a"*20+" "+"b"*20,
 "a"*20+" "+"b"*20+" "+"c"*20,
 "a"*31+" "+"b",
 "a"*32+" b",
 "a "+"b"*40,
 "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb", # 30 + 32
 "word  double  spaces  word  double  spaces  word",
 "  leading and trailing  ",
 " ".join(["x"]*100),
]
for t in tests:
    border,cols=cells(t)
    print(f"input len={len(t)} {t!r}")
    print(f" borderwidth={len(border)} cols={cols}")
PY
"}

import subprocess, json, random, string
random.seed(12345)
def partition(wordlens):
    words=[]
    for i,l in enumerate(wordlens):
        ch=string.ascii_lowercase[i%26]
        # if same char repeated across words could merged indistinguishable if separated lines? spaces preserve, each word char repeated; i cycles but line partition by split spaces returns each word token so fine even token chars repeat after 26 (use N<26)
        words.append(ch*l)
    s=" ".join(words)
    obj={"Path":s,"Version":"v1"}
    p=subprocess.run(["./executable"],input=(json.dumps(obj)+"\n").encode(),capture_output=True)
    lines=p.stdout.decode().split("\n")[3:-2]
    parts=[]
    for line in lines:
        content=line.split("|")[1][1:].rstrip()
        if content=="": parts.append([])
        else: parts.append([len(w) for w in content.split(" ")])
    return parts

data=[]
for trial in range(200):
    n=random.randint(5,18)
    lens=[random.randint(1,12) for _ in range(n)]
    if sum(lens)+n-1<=30: continue
    parts=partition(lens)
    flat=[x for part in parts for x in part]
    if flat!=lens:
        print("Mismatch reconstruction",lens,parts)
    data.append({"lens":lens,"parts":parts})
json.dump(data,open("/tmp/wrapdata.json","w"),indent=1)
print("cases",len(data))
for d in data[:20]: print(d)

    return parts

# recreate DP from fitwrap by exec (it prints? avoid)
import json

def line_len(a,i,j): return sum(a[i:j])+(j-i-1)
def dp(a,pen=0,lim=30):
    n=len(a); INF=10**18; cost=[0]*(n+1); choice=[n]*(n+1)
    for i in range(n-1,-1,-1):
        best=INF; bj=None
        for j in range(i+1,n+1):
            ll=line_len(a,i,j)
            if ll>lim:
                if j>i+1: break
                else: continue
            lc=0 if j==n else (lim-ll)**2+pen
            tot=lc+cost[j]
            if tot<best: best=tot; bj=j
        cost[i]=best; choice[i]=bj

    while i<n:
        j=choice[i]; parts.append(a[i:j]); i=j

    n=len(a); INF=999; dpv=[INF]*(n+1); dpv[n]=0; ch=[n]*(n+1)
    for i in range(n-1,-1,-1):
        for j in range(i+1,n+1):
            if line_len(a,i,j)>lim: break
            if 1+dpv[j]<dpv[i]: dpv[i]=1+dpv[j]; ch[i]=j
    return dpv[0]

        print("pen distinguishes",a,"pen0",p0,"pen100",p100)

        if found>20: break
print("found",found)

    # simplified for tests ASCII only relevant
    return 1

    return sum(rune_width(c) for c in s)
def D_width(s):
    return S_width(ANSI_RE.sub("",s))

    INF=10**18; cost=[0]*(n+1); choice=[n]*(n+1)
    for i in range(n-1,-1,-1):

import subprocess,json
def aligned(s,args=[]):
    objs=[{"Path":s,"Version":"v"},{"Path":"x"*20,"Version":"v"}]
    inp="\n".join(json.dumps(o) for o in objs)+"\n"
    p=subprocess.run(["/tmp/reference_executable"]+args,input=inp.encode(),capture_output=True)
    lines=p.stdout.decode().split("\n")
    idx=3 if not args else 2
    if len(lines)<=idx: return repr(p.stdout.decode())
    seg=lines[idx].split("|")[1]
    # first char pad; content field between pad and final pad: seg[1:-1]
    content=seg[1:]
    stripped=content.lstrip(' ')
    leading=len(content)-len(stripped)
    # right aligned if leading >0 and stripped starts s maybe (for ansi, stripped logic)
    return leading,repr(seg)

import subprocess,json,sys
REF="/tmp/reference_executable"; MINE="/tmp/my_executable"

    for cp in range(chunk_start,min(chunk_start+chunkn,end)):
        if cp in (0x0a,): continue
        if 0xd800<=cp<=0xdfff: continue
        cps.append(cp)
    objs=[{"Path":"a"*30,"Version":"v"}]
    for cp in cps:
        s=("a"+chr(cp)) if mode=="aX" else (chr(cp)+"a")
        objs.append({"Path":s,"Version":"v"})
    inp="\n".join(json.dumps(o,ensure_ascii=False) for o in objs)+"\n"
    inp=inp.encode()

    b=subprocess.run([MINE],input=inp,capture_output=True)
    if a.stdout==b.stdout: continue
    al=a.stdout.decode(errors='backslashreplace').split("\n")
    bl=b.stdout.decode(errors='backslashreplace').split("\n")
    # data start index3; al[-1] empty, border second last
    # if counts differ report chunk
    if len(al)!=len(bl):
        print("chunk line count diff",hex(chunk_start),len(al),len(bl)); continue
    for idx,cp in enumerate(cps):
        x=al[4+idx]; y=bl[4+idx]  # first data row at index3 is ref row, next at4

            diffs.append(cp)

# summarize ranges
ranges=[]
for cp in diffs:
    if ranges and ranges[-1][1]==cp-1:ranges[-1][1]=cp
    else:ranges.append([cp,cp])
for a,b in ranges:print(f"{a:04X}-{b:04X}")

end=s.index('\nconst (',start)
new='''func isZeroWidthRune(r rune) bool {
\tif isOtherMark(r) {
\t\treturn false
\t}
\tswitch {
\tcase r == 0x00ad, r == 0x070f, r == 0x180e, r == 0x2028, r == 0x2029, r == 0xfeff, r == 0xfffe, r == 0xffff:
\t\treturn true
\tcase r >= 0x200b && r <= 0x200f:
\t\treturn true
\tcase r >= 0x202a && r <= 0x202e:
\t\treturn true
\tcase r >= 0x206a && r <= 0x206f:
\t\treturn true
\tcase r >= 0xfff9 && r <= 0xfffb:
\t\treturn true
\t}
\tindex := sort.Search(len(zeroWidthRanges), func(i int) bool {
\t\treturn zeroWidthRanges[i].hi >= r
\t})
\treturn index < len(zeroWidthRanges) && zeroWidthRanges[index].lo <= r
}

    type Module struct {
        Path       string        // module path
        Query      string        // version query corresponding to this version
        Version    string        // module version
        Versions   []string      // available module versions
        Replace    *Module       // replaced by this module
        Time       *time.Time    // time version was created
        Update     *Module       // available update (with -u)
        Main       bool          // is this the main module?
        Indirect   bool          // module is only indirectly needed by main module
        Dir        string        // directory holding local copy of files, if any
        GoMod      string        // path to go.mod file describing module, if any
        GoVersion  string        // go version used in module
        Retracted  []string      // retraction information, if any (with -retracted or -u)
        Deprecated string        // deprecation message, if any (with -u)
        Error      *ModuleError  // error loading module
        Origin     any           // provenance of module
        Reuse      bool          // reuse of old module info is safe
    }

    type ModuleError struct {
        Err string // the error itself
    }

The file GoMod refers to may be outside the module directory if the
module is in the module cache or if the -modfile flag is used.

The default output is to print the module path and then
information about the version and replacement if any.
For example, 'go list -m all' might print:

    my/main/module
    golang.org/x/text v0.3.0 => /tmp/text
    rsc.io/pdf v0.1.1

The Module struct has a String method that formats this
line of output, so that the default format is equivalent
to -f '{{.String}}'.

Note that when a module has been replaced, its Replace field
describes the replacement module, and its Dir field is set to
the replacement's source code, if present. (That is, if Replace
is non-nil, then Dir is set to Replace.Dir, with no access to
the replaced source code.)

The -u flag adds information about available upgrades.
When the latest version of a given module is newer than
the current one, list -u sets the Module's Update field
to information about the newer module. list -u will also set
the module's Retracted field if the current version is retracted.
The Module's String method indicates an available upgrade by
formatting the newer version in brackets after the current version.
If a version is retracted, the string "(retracted)" will follow it.
For example, 'go list -m -u all' might print:

    my/main/module
    golang.org/x/text v0.3.0 [v0.4.0] => /tmp/text
    rsc.io/pdf v0.1.1 (retracted) [v0.1.2]

(For tools, 'go list -m -u -json all' may be more convenient to parse.)

The -versions flag causes list to set the Module's Versions field
to a list of all known versions of that module, ordered according
to semantic versioning, earliest to latest. The flag also changes
the default output format to display the module path followed by the
space-separated version list.

The -retracted flag causes list to report information about retracted
module versions. When -retracted is used with -f or -json, the Retracted
field will be set to a string explaining why the version was retracted.
The string is taken from comments on the retract directive in the
module's go.mod file. When -retracted is used with -versions, retracted
versions are listed together with unretracted versions. The -retracted
flag may be used with or without -m.

The arguments to list -m are interpreted as a list of modules, not packages.
The main module is the module containing the current directory.
The active modules are the main module and its dependencies.
With no arguments, list -m shows the main module.
With arguments, list -m shows the modules specified by the arguments.

import sys,random,json,string
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp');from difftest import compare
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]))
fails=0
for trial in range(300):
 parts=[]
 for _ in range(random.randint(0,20)):
  kind=random.random()
  if kind<0.4:
   params=';'.join(''.join(random.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(random.randint(0,5))) for __ in range(random.randint(0,4)))
   final=random.choice(string.ascii_letters+'|K@%~')
   parts.append('\x1b['+params+final)
  elif kind<0.6:
   parts.append(''.join(random.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(random.randint(0,12))))
  elif kind<0.75:
   parts.append(random.choice([' ','  ','\n','\t','\r','\x1b','\x1b[','[31m','\x1b]8;;url\x1b\\']))
  else:
   parts.append(''.join(random.choice('0123456789,.-') for _ in range(random.randint(0,8))))
 s=''.join(parts)
 inp=json.dumps({"Path":s,"Version":s})+"\n"
 if not compare(inp,[],f'ansi{trial}'):
  fails+=1
  if fails>=5:break
print('fails',fails)
PY
for sd in 1 2 3; do timeout 120 python3 /tmp/random_ansi.py $sd; done"}

# go-mod-outdated

An easy way to find outdated dependencies of your Go projects.

go-mod-outdated provides a table view of the **go list -u -m -json all** command which lists all dependencies of a Go project and their available minor and patch updates. It also provides a way to filter indirect dependencies and dependencies without updates.

## What it does

go-mod-outdated takes JSON output from `go list` and converts it into an easy-to-read table format showing:
- Module name
- Current version
- Available new version (if any)
- Whether it's a direct or indirect dependency
- Whether the timestamps are valid (new version is actually newer)

### Example

In short it turns this:

```
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/locker",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69",
	"Time": "2017-10-06T23:06:38Z",
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/locker/@v/v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69.mod"
}
{
	"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
	"Version": "v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64",
	"Time": "2017-06-26T11:06:00Z",
	"Update": {
		"Path": "github.com/BurntSushi/toml",
		"Version": "v0.3.1",
		"Time": "2018-08-15T10:47:33Z"
	},
	"GoMod": "/home/mojo/go/pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/!burnt!sushi/toml/@v/v0.0.0-20170626110600-a368813c5e64.mod"
}
```

into this:

```
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
|                  MODULE                   |               VERSION                |            NEW VERSION             | DIRECT | VALID TIMESTAMPS |
+-------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+------------------------------------+--------+------------------+
| github.com/BurntSushi/locker              | v0.0.0-20171006230638-a6e239ea1c69   |                                    | true   | true             |

```

## Installation

```
go install github.com/psampaz/go-mod-outdated@latest
```

## Usage

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:
 
```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

to see all modules in table view.

### Show only modules with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update
```

### Show only direct dependencies

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct
```

### Show only direct dependencies with updates

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct 
```

### Output as markdown table

To output a markdown compatible table, pass the `-style markdown` option:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -style markdown 
```

### Important note for Go 1.14 users

If you are using Go 1.14 with vendoring you need to pass **-mod=mod** or **-mod=readonly** to the go list command otherwise you will get the following error:

```
$ go list -u -m -json all
 
go list -m: can't determine available upgrades using the vendor directory
        (Use -mod=mod or -mod=readonly to bypass.)
```

The following will work:

```
go list -u -m -mod=mod -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

```
go list -u -m -mod=readonly -json all | go-mod-outdated
```

### Docker

In the folder where your go.mod lives run:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated
```

To use parameters just append:

```
go list -u -m -json all | docker run --rm -i psampaz/go-mod-outdated -update
```

### CI pipelines

Using the -ci flag will make the command exit with non-zero code, breaking your CI pipelines if outdated dependencies are found.

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail if **any direct or indirect** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -ci
```

If you want to make your CI pipeline fail **only if a direct** dependency is outdated use the following:

```
go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -ci
```

### Command-line flags

Use the **-h** or **-help** flag to see all available options:

```
$ go-mod-outdated -help

Usage of go-mod-outdated:
  -direct
        List only direct modules
  -update
        List only modules with updates
  -ci
        Non-zero exit code when at least one outdated dependency was found
  -style string
        Output style, pass 'markdown' for a Markdown table (default "default")
```

### Shortcut aliases

If **go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update -direct** seems too difficult to remember, you can create shortcuts using aliases:

```
alias gmo="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated"

alias gmod="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct"

alias gmou="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -update"

alias gmodu="go list -u -m -json all | go-mod-outdated -direct -update"
```  

## Understanding the output

### VALID TIMESTAMPS column

There are cases where the updated version reported by the go list command is actually older than the current one. go-mod-outdated includes a **VALID TIMESTAMPS** column which indicates when this happens, helping you avoid upgrading to a version that might break your application.

### Important note about upgrading

Upgrading an application is the responsibility of the application maintainer. Semantic versioning provides a way to indicate breaking changes, but everything relies on each module developer applying correct version tags. Unless there is a fully automated way to detect breaking changes in a codebase, a good practice to avoid surprises is to write tests and avoid dependencies on modules that are not well maintained and documented.
